conditions.electrolyte: not restated; the thesis electrolysis solution is 0.1 M K2SO4 + 0.05 M KNO3 (sections 5.1, 5.3)
conditions.cell_divided: Teflon cell, Nafion 117 (H+ form), 20 mL catholyte and 20 mL anolyte (ch. 4, printed p. 67)
conditions.cell_undivided: one compartment removed, 20 mL total (ch. 4, printed p. 67)
conditions.anode: not restated here (ch. 4 describes the auxiliary electrode)

text_translated: Printed p. 116: the gaseous selectivity in the undivided cell came from subtracting the NO2- and NH3 selectivities from 100 %. RE is lower in every undivided-cell case and the NO2-/NH3 selectivities fall, so the gaseous selectivity rises. Printed p. 117: selectivities did not change significantly when electrolysis was extended to 24 h; the NH3 decrease in the undivided cell was attributed to anodic oxidation to gaseous products and nitrate, and the lower RE to nitrate formed at the anode. Anodic oxidation of 0.1 M K2SO4 + 0.05 M (NH4)2SO4 on Pt at 2.3 and 2.5 V vs Ag/AgCl removed 12 and 15 % of the ammonia with 85 and 92 % selectivity to nitrate; no nitrite detected.

checks.undivided_cell_closure: all undivided-cell rows sum to 100.0 %, as expected for gases by difference
checks.divided_cell_closure: divided-cell rows sum to 85.7-98.6 %, so their gaseous column is not by difference
